title: Graded Degradation Prober: multi-tier failover and load-shed validation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build and run a repeatable chaos harness that injects graded degradations across layers (region loss, GPU pool exhaustion, downstream blackholes) to validate SLO behaviour, circuit-breaker correctness, and load-shedding policies. The probe must exercise canary and bulk failover paths, measure time-to-routing-stability, and confirm graceful degradation (fallback model variants or soft-deny) for customer workloads.
objective: Validate that routing, autoscale, and admission-control layers keep customer-visible error rates and p95/p99 latencies within SLOs during staged region and dependency degradations, and that circuit breakers and load-shedding trigger and recover without cascading failures.
test_scenarios: Scenario A: Single-region abrupt loss: advertise region down and simulate control-plane ejection for 60s while routing rebalanced to other regions.
Scenario B: GPU pool starvation: reserve 90% of a single region's GPU capacity with synthetic jobs to force queueing and kernel-level queuing pressure.
Scenario C: Downstream blackhole: introduce latency spikes and 100% drop towards a critical dependency (model-compiler-service) to validate circuit breaker and fallback to cached artifacts.

Scenario D: Compound progressive degradation: sequence of small failures (5%, then 20%, then 60% capacity loss) over 20 minutes to validate rolling back of canary and progressive load-shed thresholds.
Scenario E: Network partition + cold-cache pressure: partition half the regional proxies and purge KV cache to see cold-warm startup behavior and tail latencies.
runbook_steps: 1) Spin up isolated test tenant with traffic generator in staging that mimics production token mix and batching characteristics.
2) Warm model caches and validate baseline SLOs for 30 minutes.
3) Execute Scenario A: mark region R-us-west as offline via failure-injector, monitor routing table, and block egress to region for 60s.
4) Execute Scenario B after recovery: allocate synthetic GPU jobs to saturate GPU pool and observe admission-control backpressure and queue lengths.
5) Execute Scenario C concurrently: throttle dependency endpoints and toggle circuit-breaker thresholds to test trip/duration behavior.
6) Run Scenario D to test progressive policies: gradually increase injected failures and observe automatic rollout/rollback behavior for model variant routing.
7) After each scenario: collect traces, logs, latency histograms, token counts, and error taxonomy; run automated assertions against SLO criteria.
8) If hard SLOs are violated: stop test, capture post-mortem artifacts, run immediate mitigation (route traffic to dedicated pool), and create follow-up issue.
9) Publish findings to the resilience docs and schedule remediation with owners of affected subsystems.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline validation: test tenant meets pre-injection SLOs for 30 minutes.
During single-region loss: customer-visible error rate remains <0.5% and p99 latency increase <2x baseline within 3 minutes of region ejection.
GPU exhaustion: admission-control drops are correctly attributed and labeled; degraded requests are either soft-denied with explanatory error or routed to fallback variants per policy.
Circuit breaker correctness: dependent-service blackholes cause predictable trip events and traffic routed to fallback caches or alternate endpoints with no silent retries causing overload.
Progressive degradation: rollouts automatically throttle model variant traffic in accordance with policy thresholds and recover once health is restored.
No silent customer data loss: all dropped requests are accounted for in metrics and logs and appear in the incident audit trail.
Artifacts and dashboards: a reproducible dashboard for each scenario with pinned time windows and alert rule snapshots is published.
